Schnittstelle Tree<A>

Typparameter:
A - the type of elements held in the tree
Alle Superschnittstellen:
Visitable<Tree<A>>
Alle bekannten Unterschnittstellen:
BinaryTree<A>
Alle bekannten Implementierungsklassen:
AVLTree, AVLTree.Leaf, AVLTree.Node, RedBlackTree, RedBlackTree.Leaf, RedBlackTree.Node
public interface Tree<A> extends Visitable<Tree<A>>

A generic, hierarchical tree structure holding elements of type A. The tree is designed to be immutable and provides core operations for insertion, deletion, and search.

As a Visitable type, it supports externalised operations via the Visitor pattern, allowing for flexible traversal and processing of tree nodes.

    • isLeaf

    • height

      int height()

      Returns the height of this tree node.

      The height is defined as the number of nodes along the longest path from this node down to the farthest leaf. A terminal/empty node typically has a height of 0, while a single leaf node has a height of 1.

      Gibt zurück:
      the height of this tree
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • insert

      @NonNull Tree<A> insert(@NonNull A element)

      Inserts the specified element into the tree.

      Contract: element must not be null. The method returns a new tree instance containing the element, preserving the original tree's immutability.

      Parameter:
      element - the element to insert; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a new tree instance containing the element
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if element is null

    • children

      @NonNull List<? extends Tree<A>> children()

      Returns the direct child nodes of the current tree node.

      The returned list contains the immediate subtrees. For terminal nodes (leaves or empty ends), this list is empty.

      Gibt zurück:
      a list of child nodes; may be empty but not null

    • welcome

      default <V extends Visitor<? super Tree<A>>> @NonNull V welcome(@NonNull V visitor)

      Accepts the given visitor and applies it to this tree node.

      Contract: visitor must not be null. The returned visitor is the same instance passed in, allowing fluent chaining.
